candidate_profile.description: The candidate is strong and commercially grounded. They interpret market share correctly, diagnose the shrinking-market and pricing problem well, and recommend cost reduction plus diversification with solid logic and structure.
behaviour_rules: Open with a concise recap and explicitly question what rising market share means.
Use a clear framework covering volume, price, cost, industry demand, and competition.
Quickly establish that costs are steady and that the real issue must be on the revenue-quality side.
Recognize that volume is only slightly up, while pricing pressure is reducing margin per unit.
Interpret competitor exits as evidence of industry saturation and unattractive economics.
Connect lower demand for preservatives to broader consumer movement toward fresh foods.
Conclude that the client is gaining share largely because the market is shrinking and competitors are disappearing, not because the business is truly stronger.
Recommend aggressive cost reduction, collaborative purchasing leverage where feasible, and diversification into more attractive chemical categories.

expected_issues: May be slightly less crisp than an excellent candidate when synthesizing the full industry story into one decisive statement.
Could go deeper on the practical sequencing of cost actions and diversification.
expected_feedback_points: Strong interpretation of market share in context.
Strong diagnosis of shrinking-market price pressure rather than cost inflation.
Strong connection between fresh-food substitution and industry decline.
Strong recommendation to reduce costs and diversify the portfolio.
To reach excellent level, make the final synthesis even tighter and more executive-ready.
